name: language-rooting-evidence
body:
Verified facts on this branch (code graph + source reads), and the Human decision they support.

HUMAN DECISION (do not re-litigate): language rooting — a `Language` code-graph node kind and language-rooted FQNs, folded into the scanner-optimisation change-set.

(1) Module FQNs are emitted verbatim with no cross-language namespace: src/ingest.rs buffers `Record::Module { fqn }` and Pass B2 inserts it unchanged (src/ingest.rs:647-670).

(2) The ingestor SILENTLY SHADOWS a module whose FQN is already claimed (module-vs-module or module-vs-type): Pass B2 `if seen.contains_key(fqn) { shadowed.insert(fqn); shadowed_modules += 1; continue; }` drops the module and its `Module→File` edge is pruned by the dangling-edge cleanup; src/main.rs logs "{} module(s) shadowed by a type of the same name (package/type collision; type wins)" (src/main.rs:1446-1449). This is silent data loss — the module is simply absent from the graph, with no error.

(3) Only same-kind collisions fail loudly: `claim` (src/ingest.rs:88-96) panics "FQN collision: `{fqn}` claimed by both `{prev}` and `{id}`", and function-vs-function panics at the Pass B insertion (src/ingest.rs:614-615); a struct silently shadows a function (`shadowed_functions`). So today a cross-language module collision is a silent drop while a cross-language same-kind symbol collision is a hard panic — both are the class of failure the disjoint language roots remove.

(4) Symbols render `parent.name` from the record's `parent`, which for a top-level declaration IS the verbatim module FQN (`render_function_fqns`, src/ingest.rs:98-138; struct insertion, src/ingest.rs:229). Rooting the module therefore requires rooting the declaration parent too, or symbols would hang off an unrooted parent.

(5) `NodeKind` (src/graph.rs:53-92) has no Language variant; `valid_contains_pair` (src/ingest.rs:984-1012) has no `(Language, Module)` pair; the DB schema/rel-table pairs are built in src/load.rs (`create_schema` / `spec_rel_pairs`) and the export in `write_graph_jsonl`.

(6) The code universe that validates authored `implemented-by` targets is the scanned graph / `graph.jsonl` (src/layers.rs `classify_code_ref`; `apg.artifacts.code_universes_from_export`). Every authored `implemented-by` edge on this branch targets a bare code FQN (e.g. solution.container.ingestor → apg.ingest.ingest, solution.component.language-detector → apg.auto_detect_languages, solution.component.code-type-classifier → apg.classify.builtin_code_type). Rooting the module FQNs shifts all of them, so every existing target is DRIFT until migrated (see requirements.requirement.implemented-by-migration).

(7) Unaffected by design: `UnresolvedTarget` FQNs (foreign symbol names, not project identities) and `code_type` (path-based).

recorded.
